segments.en: Bread.

segments.en: Bread is an important ingredient here.

segments.en: You need to remember one thing.
segments.zh: 你需要记住一件事。

segments.en: Use the bread according to the following criteria, freshness, crumb and color.
segments.zh: 选择面包时，要考虑以下标准：新鲜度、内部组织和色泽。

segments.en: If you want a closed sandwich, I recommend you first toast your bread in a toaster or oven or grill it slightly until it gets a light brown color.
segments.zh: 如果要做两片面包夹馅的三明治，建议先用烤面包机或烤箱把面包烤至浅棕色，也可以稍微炙烤一下。

segments.en: Now that our bread is ready, let's talk about the ingredients.
segments.zh: 既然我们的面包准备好了，让我们谈谈成分。

segments.en: Of course, each person's palate is different, but I'm going to give you a few tips that you'll be able to use when turning any sandwich into the perfect sandwich.
segments.zh: 当然，每个人的味觉都不同，但我会给你一些技巧，你可以在把任何三明治变成完美的三明治时使用这些技巧。

segments.en: I would strongly recommend you put fresh vegetables in your sandwich.
segments.zh: 我强烈建议你在三明治里放新鲜的蔬菜。

segments.en: Do not undervalue them as they play a big role in forming the taste and will make the sandwich more refreshing and light.
segments.zh: 不要低估它们，因为它们在形成味道方面起着重要作用，并且会使三明治更清爽和清淡。

segments.en: The best choices here are evident.
segments.zh: 这里的最佳选择是显而易见的。

segments.en: Cucumbers, tomatoes, onions, sweet pepper or chili, lettuce, and of course herbs.
segments.zh: 黄瓜、西红柿、洋葱、甜椒或辣椒、生菜，当然还有香草。

segments.en: You can't go wrong with them.
segments.zh: 你不会出错的。

segments.en: As for aubergines, mushrooms and asparagus, I would recommend you first grill them slightly with a little touch of olive oil.
segments.zh: 至于茄子、蘑菇和芦笋，我建议你先用一点橄榄油稍微烤一下。

segments.en: Last but not least, we have a wide variety of condiments that we can add to our perfect sandwich.
segments.zh: 最后但并非最不重要的一点是，我们有各种各样的调味品，可以添加到我们完美的三明治中。

segments.en: We can be subtle and add just a touch of salt and pepper, or we can combine mustard sauce, mayonnaise, ketchup, or even caviar to achieve a stronger flavor.
segments.zh: 想要清淡些，可以只放少许盐和胡椒；也可以搭配芥末酱、蛋黄酱、番茄酱，甚至鱼子酱，让口味更浓郁。

segments.en: It's always a good idea to cut your sandwich in triangles or manageable pieces to avoid all your ingredients falling out and staining your shirt.
segments.zh: 最好把三明治切成三角形或方便拿取的小块，免得里面的食材掉出来弄脏衬衫。

segments.en: That's all the time we have for today, but join us next time where we'll be going over how to make the perfect lasagna.

segments.en: Oh, and mustard as well.
segments.zh: 哦，还有芥末。

segments.en: These are all condiments.
segments.zh: 这些都是调味品。

segments.en: So in different parts of the world, they have different kinds of condiments.
segments.zh: 所以在世界不同的地方，他们有不同种类的调味品。

segments.en: I've seen, for example, a lot of vinegar in Asia.
segments.zh: 例如，我在亚洲见过很多醋。

segments.en: You can also have hot pepper flakes like in Europe.
segments.zh: 你也可以像欧洲一样吃辣椒片。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: The condiments that you add to your sandwich are varied.
segments.zh: 您添加到三明治中的调味品多种多样。

segments.en: I've seen people put all types of condiments in their sandwich.
segments.zh: 我见过人们在他们的三明治里放了所有类型的调味品。

segments.en: And, for example, one that may be a little bit strange or maybe a little bit more expensive condiment is caviar.
segments.zh: 例如，可能有点奇怪或可能更昂贵的调味品是鱼子酱。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So caviar is not always considered a condiment.
segments.zh: 所以鱼子酱并不总是被认为是一种调味品。

segments.en: It can be, but it can also be eaten alone.
segments.zh: 可以，但也可以单独食用。

segments.en: But it's basically just fish eggs.
segments.zh: 但这基本上就是鱼卵。

segments.en: They're little fish eggs.
segments.zh: 它们是小鱼卵。

segments.en: Very small.
segments.zh: 很小。

segments.en: It always usually, in people's mind, it's kind of like a fancy food, very luxurious, very expensive.
segments.zh: 通常，在人们的心目中，它有点像花哨的食物，非常豪华，非常昂贵。

segments.en: Well, it can be very expensive if you get like beluga caviar.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果您像 Beluga 鱼子酱一样，它可能会非常昂贵。

segments.en: A lot of caviar comes from the Caucasus and Russia and Ukraine, these places.
segments.zh: 很多鱼子酱来自高加索和俄罗斯和乌克兰，这些地方。

segments.en: And it's very, very salty in flavor.
segments.zh: 它的味道非常非常咸。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So that is also considered a condiment in our case because we're using it for a sandwich, right?
segments.zh: 所以这在我们的案例中也被认为是一种调味品，因为我们将它用作三明治，对吧？

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So a lot of words there, a lot of interesting things going on in our sandwich.
segments.zh: 所以那里有很多话，我们的三明治里发生了很多有趣的事情。

segments.en: Why don't we move on now to Fluency Builder where we're going to take a look at some phrases.
segments.zh: 我们不妨现在进入流利表达，来看一些短语。

segments.en: Fluency Builder
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So let's go back to the very beginning of the dialogue when she said, all right, let's start with the basics.
segments.zh: 所以让我们回到对话的开头，她说，好吧，让我们从基础开始。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: The basics is a set phrase in this context.
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，基础是一个固定的短语。

segments.en: We can say this about many different things, but the basics basically refers to the most simple ingredients or the most simple elements.
segments.zh: 我们可以说很多不同的东西，但基础基本上是指最简单的成分或最简单的元素。

segments.en: In this case, bread or meat.
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，面包或肉类。

segments.en: But you can also talk about the basics in other contexts like clothes shopping.
segments.zh: 但您也可以在其他情况下谈论基本知识，例如衣服购物。

segments.en: Like when school started when I was a kid, my mom always used to buy me the basics.
segments.zh: 就像我小时候开学时一样，我妈妈总是给我买基础的东西。

segments.en: So T-shirts and socks.
segments.zh: 所以T恤和袜子。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So I guess the basics are the absolute necessary things.
segments.zh: 所以我想基础是绝对必要的东西。

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: Right?
segments.zh: 对吧？

segments.en: And also very simple.
segments.zh: 而且也很简单。

segments.en: So for example, if you talk about dancing, the basics would be maybe a certain sequence of steps that important, essential.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，如果您谈论跳舞，基础可能是重要的、必不可少的一系列步骤。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And would caviar be a part of the basics, for example?
segments.zh: 例如，鱼子酱会成为基础的一部分吗？

segments.en: No, no, no.
segments.zh: 不，不，不。

segments.en: No, that's an extra.
segments.zh: 不，这是额外的。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this is what we refer to when we say the basics.
segments.zh: 所以这就是我们在说基础时所指的。

segments.en: Now our chef, when she continued talking about her sandwich, she said, I would strongly recommend you use fresh vegetables in your sandwich.
segments.zh: 现在我们的厨师，当她继续谈论她的三明治时，她说，我强烈建议你在三明治中使用新鲜蔬菜。

segments.en: Okay, so you can say I would recommend this, but to strongly recommend is to have a very, very strong feeling about something.
segments.zh: 好的，所以你可以说我会推荐这个，但强烈推荐是对某事有一种非常非常强烈的感觉。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: You're saying to the person basically do it.
segments.zh: 你是在对那个人说基本上这样做。

segments.en: You must.
segments.zh: 你必须。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So if maybe your friend is sick, you can say something like, I would strongly recommend you go to the doctor today.
segments.zh: 所以如果你的朋友生病了，你可以说，我强烈建议你今天去看医生。

segments.en: That means you really, really should go to the doctor.
segments.zh: 这意味着你真的，真的应该去看医生。

segments.en: I would be upset if you didn't.
segments.zh: 如果你不这样做，我会很沮丧。

segments.en: It's kind of formal though.
segments.zh: 虽然有点正式。

segments.en: It seems like you would maybe use it with your boss or maybe with a person you don't really know that well, but with your friend you would say, I really think you should go to the doctor.
segments.zh: 看起来你可能会和你的老板一起使用它，或者可能和一个你不太了解的人一起使用它，但你会说，你会说，我真的认为你应该去看医生。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: But you can say it in both contexts, but yeah, definitely more of a formal thing.
segments.zh: 但是你可以在两种情况下都说，但是，肯定更像是正式的事情。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we strongly recommend that you, yeah, okay.
segments.zh: 所以我们强烈建议你，是的，好的。

segments.en: All right, so now for our last phrase, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，现在我们的最后一句话，对吧？

segments.en: Where are we?
segments.zh: 我们在哪儿？

segments.en: Last but not least.
segments.zh: 最后一点也同样重要。

segments.en: Last but not least.
segments.zh: 最后一点也同样重要。

segments.en: So now moving on to our next phrase, when she started talking about the condiment, she said, last but not least, we have a wide variety of condiments.
segments.zh: 所以现在继续我们的下一个短语，当她开始谈论调味品时，她说，最后但并非最不重要的一点是，我们有各种各样的调味品。

segments.en: Okay, this is a very, very common phrase.
segments.zh: 好的，这是一个非常非常常见的短语。

segments.en: It's a set phrase.
segments.zh: 这是一个固定的短语。

segments.en: You will hear these words together very often.
segments.zh: 你会经常一起听到这些话。

segments.en: Last but not least.
segments.zh: 最后一点也同样重要。

segments.en: What could this possibly mean?
segments.zh: 这可能意味着什么？

segments.en: So obviously last means the last step here.
segments.zh: 所以显然最后一步在这里意味着最后一步。

segments.en: The last point.
segments.zh: 最后一点。

segments.en: But why not least?
segments.zh: 但为什么不是最少呢？

segments.en: Well, it's not least important.
segments.zh: 好吧，这并非最不重要。

segments.en: Just because it's last, it doesn't mean that it's not important.
segments.zh: 仅仅因为它是最后一个，并不意味着它不重要。

segments.en: Okay, so maybe there are many people who have to give presentations in school and I'm the very, very last person to go.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以也许有很多人必须在学校做演讲，而我是最后一个要去的人。

segments.en: The teacher will say, last but not least, Catherine.
segments.zh: 老师会说，最后但同样重要的是，凯瑟琳。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Makes me feel better.
segments.zh: 让我感觉好多了。

segments.en: Because you're saying you're last, but it doesn't mean you're not important.
segments.zh: 因为你说你是最后一个，但这并不意味着你不重要。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So when you want to make sure that the last point of your presentation or what you're talking about is not ignored or you just want to make sure that everyone knows that it's also very important, you say, last but not least.
segments.zh: 因此，当您想确保演示文稿的最后一点或您正在谈论的内容没有被忽视时，或者您只是想确保每个人都知道这也非常重要，您说，最后但并非最不重要。

segments.en: Great.
segments.zh: 太好了。

segments.en: All right, and now last but not least, the end of Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 好吧，现在最后但并非最不重要的是，流利表达的终结。

segments.en: We're going to close off with this little phrase.
segments.zh: 我们将以这个小短语结束。

segments.en: When she was talking about salt and pepper, she said, a touch of salt and pepper.
segments.zh: 当她谈到盐和胡椒时，她说，放一点盐和胡椒。

segments.en: Okay, a touch of salt and pepper is basically a measure.
segments.zh: 好吧，一点盐和胡椒基本上是一种衡量标准。

segments.en: It's not a lot.
segments.zh: 这不是很多。

segments.en: It's very little amount of salt and pepper.
segments.zh: 盐和胡椒粉的量很少。

segments.en: So we can say a touch.
segments.zh: 所以我们可以说一点。

segments.en: So it's not really a specific quantity though, right?
segments.zh: 所以它不是一个特定的数量，对吧？

segments.en: We're not saying like a spoon of salt and pepper.
segments.zh: 我们不是说像一勺盐和胡椒粉。

segments.en: Not at all.
segments.zh: 一点也不。

segments.en: It basically means a little bit.
segments.zh: 它基本上意味着一点点。

segments.en: A little bit.
segments.zh: 有一点。

segments.en: So you're just saying, maybe you'll hear this in maybe a cooking show or you'll read it in books when they'll say a pinch of salt or a touch of salt or a dash of salt.
segments.zh: 所以你只是在说，也许你会在烹饪节目中听到这一点，或者当他们说一小撮盐、少许盐或少许盐时，你会在书中读到它。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: You could even say it about other things.
segments.zh: 你甚至可以说其他事情。

segments.en: For example, if my friend just wrote this article and he wanted me to read it, I say, it's a really good article, but it could use a touch of humor.
segments.zh: 例如，如果我的朋友刚刚写了这篇文章，他想让我读它，我说，这是一篇非常好的文章，但它可以使用一丝幽默感。

segments.en: I think maybe if you made it a little bit funny, it would be better.
segments.zh: 我想也许如果你让它有点有趣，那会更好。

segments.en: Or maybe if you're painting your house, you can say, oh, I think a touch of red paint would look really nice on this wall.
segments.zh: 或者，如果你在粉刷你的房子，你可以说，哦，我认为这堵墙上的一抹红色油漆会看起来非常漂亮。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: A little bit of red paint would be good.
segments.zh: 一点红色的油漆会很好。

segments.en: Okay. So a touch of, a really, really good phrase.
segments.zh: 好的。 所以一点，一个非常非常好的短语。

segments.en: It makes you sound very natural.
segments.zh: 它让你听起来很自然。

segments.en: Okay, so that's all the time we have for today.
segments.zh: 好的，这就是我们今天所拥有的所有时间。

segments.en: But before we go, let's listen to the dialogue again.
segments.zh: 但在我们走之前，让我们再听一次对话。

segments.en: Welcome to our show.
segments.zh: 欢迎收看我们的节目。

segments.en: Today, I'm going to show you how to make the perfect mouthwatering sandwich.
segments.zh: 今天，我将向您展示如何制作完美令人垂涎的三明治。

segments.en: Are you ready?
segments.zh: 你准备好了吗？

segments.en: Let's get started.
segments.zh: 我们开始吧。

segments.en: Let's start with the basics.
segments.zh: 让我们从基础开始。

segments.en: Bread.
segments.zh: 面包。

segments.en: Bread is an important ingredient here.
segments.zh: 面包是这里的重要成分。

segments.en: You need to remember one thing.
segments.zh: 你需要记住一件事。

segments.en: Choose the bread according to the following criteria.
segments.zh: 根据以下标准选择面包。

segments.en: Freshness, crumb, and color.
segments.zh: 新鲜度、面包屑和颜色。

segments.en: If you want a closed sandwich, I recommend you first toast your bread in a toaster or oven or grill it slightly until it gets a light brown color.
segments.zh: 如果要做两片面包夹馅的三明治，建议先用烤面包机或烤箱把面包烤至浅棕色，也可以稍微炙烤一下。

segments.en: Now that our bread is ready, let's talk about the ingredients.
segments.zh: 既然我们的面包准备好了，让我们谈谈成分。

segments.en: Of course, each person's palate is different, but I'm going to give you a few tips that you'll be able to use when turning any sandwich into the perfect sandwich.
segments.zh: 当然，每个人的味觉都不同，但我会给你一些技巧，你可以在把任何三明治变成完美的三明治时使用这些技巧。

segments.en: I would strongly recommend you put fresh vegetables in your sandwich.
segments.zh: 我强烈建议你在三明治里放新鲜的蔬菜。

segments.en: Do not undervalue them as they play a big role in forming the taste and will make the sandwich more refreshing and light.
segments.zh: 不要低估它们，因为它们在形成味道方面起着重要作用，并且会使三明治更清爽和清淡。

segments.en: The best choices here are evident.
segments.zh: 这里的最佳选择是显而易见的。

segments.en: Cucumbers, tomatoes, onions, sweet pepper or chili, lettuce, and of course, herbs.
segments.zh: 黄瓜、西红柿、洋葱、甜椒或辣椒、生菜，当然还有香草。

segments.en: You can't go wrong with them.
segments.zh: 你不会出错的。

segments.en: As for aubergines, mushrooms, and asparagus, I would recommend you first grill them slightly with a little touch of olive oil.
segments.zh: 至于茄子、蘑菇和芦笋，我建议你先用一点橄榄油稍微烤一下。

segments.en: Last but not least, we have a wide variety of condiments that we can add to our perfect sandwich.
segments.zh: 最后但并非最不重要的一点是，我们有各种各样的调味品，可以添加到我们完美的三明治中。

segments.en: We can be subtle and add just a touch of salt and pepper, or we can combine mustard sauce, mayonnaise, ketchup, or even caviar to achieve a stronger flavor.
segments.zh: 想要清淡些，可以只放少许盐和胡椒；也可以搭配芥末酱、蛋黄酱、番茄酱，甚至鱼子酱，让口味更浓郁。

segments.en: It's always a good idea to cut your sandwich in triangles or manageable pieces to avoid all your ingredients falling out and staining your shirt.
segments.zh: 最好把三明治切成三角形或方便拿取的小块，免得里面的食材掉出来弄脏衬衫。

segments.en: That's all the time we have for today, but join us next time where we'll be going over how to make the perfect lasagna.
segments.zh: 今天的节目就到这里，下次我们会教大家制作完美的意式千层面，记得收看。

segments.en: Till next time!
segments.zh: 下次再见！

segments.en: Alright, so talking about sandwich, this really reminds me of making sandwiches at home.
segments.zh: 好吧，说到三明治，这真的让我想起了在家做三明治。

segments.en: Grilled cheese sandwich.
segments.zh: 烤奶酪三明治。

segments.en: We didn't really talk about it here, but I think it's my favorite sandwich.
segments.zh: 我们在这里并没有真正谈论它，但我认为这是我最喜欢的三明治。

segments.en: The grilled cheese sandwich.
segments.zh: 烤奶酪三明治。

segments.en: It's very easy to make.
segments.zh: 这很容易制作。

segments.en: Just two pieces of bread and cheese inside.
segments.zh: 里面只有两块面包和奶酪。

segments.en: Do you use butter, though?
segments.zh: 不过，你用黄油吗？

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: So you have to butter the bread, and so when you grill it, it gets really nice and brown.
segments.zh: 所以你必须在面包上涂黄油，所以当你烤的时候，它会变得非常漂亮和棕色。

segments.en: Actually, I'm not a very big sandwich fan when I'm having, for example, a meal like lunch.
segments.zh: 其实，如果要吃午餐这种正餐，我不太喜欢三明治。

segments.en: I don't know.
segments.zh: 我不知道。

segments.en: I think I need something more solid than just a sandwich at times.
segments.zh: 我觉得有时候我需要比三明治更实在的东西。

segments.en: Interesting.
segments.zh: 有意思。

segments.en: I had a sandwich for dinner last night.
segments.zh: 我昨晚晚餐吃了一个三明治。

segments.en: Yeah?
segments.zh: 怎么了？

segments.en: I had an egg salad sandwich.
segments.zh: 我吃了一个鸡蛋沙拉三明治。

segments.en: So you had egg salad inside two pieces of bread.
segments.zh: 所以你在两块面包里放了鸡蛋沙拉。

segments.en: That's right, but the bread I had was French bread, so that long, thin bread was very crunchy, very delicious.
segments.zh: 没错，但我吃的面包是法式面包，所以长而薄的面包非常松脆，非常美味。

segments.en: But actually, I like sandwiches for dinner.
segments.zh: 但实际上，我喜欢晚餐吃三明治。

segments.en: They are a little bit lighter.
segments.zh: 它们比较清淡一些。

segments.en: When you're having a big meal, it just seems like, although maybe sometimes places give you very big, heavy sandwiches that have ham and salami and just a lot of things in there, so they're very, very filling.
segments.zh: 当你吃一顿大餐时，虽然有时餐馆会给你很大、很顶饱的三明治，里面有火腿、意大利腊肠，还有一大堆东西，所以非常非常顶饱。

segments.en: That's very true. Like a meatball sub, for example, is a very heavy sandwich.
segments.zh: 确实如此。比如肉丸潜艇三明治就是一个很顶饱的三明治。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: But sandwiches come in all shapes and sizes.
segments.zh: 但是三明治有各种形状和大小。

segments.en: You can make basically any sandwich that your brain can think of.
segments.zh: 你基本上可以做任何你的大脑能想到的三明治。

segments.en: And so we hope that you've learned some words for talking about sandwiches today.
segments.zh: 所以我们希望你今天学到了一些谈论三明治的词。

segments.en: Of course, if you have any questions or comments or you want to share with us your very favorite sandwich, you should do so on EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 当然，如果您有任何问题或意见，或者您想与我们分享您最喜欢的三明治，您应该在 Englishpod.com 上这样做。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: We'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 到时候在那里见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
